The reproductive biology of the Vermiculated sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus has been examined in several introduced populations across tropical and subtropical watersheds. At a stable water temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C], females exhibit a gonadosomatic index (GSI) of 6% [GSI = 6%]. This relatively low index suggests an energetic strategy that balances sustained somatic growth with periodic gamete production. Field studies report that the onset of exogenous feeding occurs approximately 11.3 days [ab = approximately 11.3 days] after egg deposition at this same thermal regime, marking the point at which yolk reserves are exhausted and free-swimming larvae must a at a temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]ctively forage. The intervening period includes roughly 1.8 days for embryonic development and hatching, followed by a lecithotrophic phase during which the yolk-sac larva relies entirely on endogenous nutrients. This relatively compressed pre-feeding interval is consistent with the rapid early development observed in other loricariid catfishes that colonize warm, productive environments.

Life-history surveys across multiple invaded drainages in Florida and Mexico indicate that the species attains a substantial body size, with the ultimate total length reaching 70 cm [Li = 70 cm] in older, well-conditioned individuals. This large adult size places P. disjunctivus among the larger members of its genus and correlates with a high ultimate wet weight, estimated at 6800 grams [Wwi = 6800 grams] for fully grown specimens based on length–weight regressions derived from robust sample sizes. These regressions reveal a strong positive allometry, with mass increasing disproportionately faster than length, a pattern typical of benthic fishes that develop thick bony plates and substantial visceral fat stores over their lifetimes. The capacity to reach such an extreme mass likely confers advantages in competition for shelter sites and in defense against certain aquatic predators, though it also imposes higher absolute metabolic demands. Ecological data further indicate that these maximum dimensions are achieved only after many years of continuous growth under favorable thermal conditions where food is abundant and intraspecific competition remains moderate.

Sexual maturation in P. disjunctivus occurs well before the attainment of maximum size, as individuals become reproductively active at a total length of 31 cm [Lp = 31 cm]. This body length corresponds to a wet weight at puberty of 591 grams [Wwp = 591 grams], calculated from the allometric scaling relationship and representing a point at which roughly twenty percent of the ultimate body mass has been accrued. The divergence between the length at puberty and the asymptotic length underscores a life-history strategy in which reproductive effort begins relatively early in the growth trajectory, a common pattern among invasive loricariids that face size-dependent mortality risks. Histological examination of gonadal tissue from individuals captured across this size threshold confirms the presence of developing oocytes and spermatocytes, validating the morphological criterion. Comparisons with congeneric species suggest that this pubertal length is near the lower end of the range for the genus, potentially facilitating rapid population establishment in newly invaded habitats.

Reproduction in this species is characterized by iteroparity and nest-guarding behavior, with spawning occurring in burrows excavated into stream banks. The earliest developmental stages are encapsulated within an adhesive, demersal egg measuring approximately 1.7 mm in diameter. Based on this egg dimension, the wet weight at birth for a newly emerged yolk-sac larva is 0.0026 grams [Wwb = 0.0026 grams], a value derived from the geometric relationship for a spherical egg. This tiny initial mass imposes a tight constraint on the duration of the endotrophic phase, as the limited yolk reserves must sustain the larva through hatching and early organogenesis until the onset of exogenous feeding. Field observations at 25 °C [T = 25 °C] indicate that the age at birth, defined as the period from fertilization to the completion of hatching, is approximately 11.3 days [ab = approximately 11.3 days], following the initial cleavage and gastrulation stages. The rapid depletion of the yolk sac is a critical bottleneck for recruitment success, particularly in variable thermal environments.

Maximum longevity under natural conditions for P. disjunctivus has been estimated at 6 years in populations inhabiting stable, warm-water systems, a figure derived from recapture studies of marked individuals and validated by otolith increment analysis. This value of 6 years [am = 6 years] at a water temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C] is consistent with the reported lifespans of several other large-bodied loricariids, reflecting an overall life-history pace that balances moderately rapid growth to a large size with an extended period of reproductive activity. The attainment of the ultimate total length of 70 cm [Li = 70 cm] and the corresponding ultimate wet weight of 6800 grams [Wwi = 6800 grams] requires the majority of this six-year span, with asymptotic size typically reached during the fourth or fifth year. Comparative analyses across the genus suggest that this lifespan is near the median for siluriform fishes of equivalent maximum mass, though it remains shorter than that of some related species with slower growth trajectories.
